contents.text: Many paragraphs begin with a topic sentence. A topic sentence tells the reader what the paragraph is about.

header.text: For example, maybe your paragraph is about how big sharks can be. This would be a good topic sentence:

text.text: Sharks are some of the largest animals in the sea.

header.text: Your topic sentence should not be too broad. "Too broad" means that the sentence doesn't tell you exactly what the paragraph is about. It doesn't give enough detail.

text.text: There are many different kinds of sharks.

header.text: Your topic sentence should not be too narrow. "Too narrow" means that the sentence tells only about a detail.

text.text: The basking shark can be over thirty feet long.

header.text: Your topic sentence should not be off topic. "Off topic" means that the sentence doesn't match the paragraph well. It tells about something else.

text.text: Sharks can be dangerous.

pieces.text: The paragraph is about seeing rocks shaped like bowling balls at a beach.

text.text: You can spot sea otters and other animals at Bowling Ball Beach.
